Explained: How mutual fund SIPs harness the power of compounding to build wealth
articles.summary: Compounding is one of the most effective ways to build long-term wealth. When paired with Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) in mutual funds, it allows investors to grow their money over time through regular investments and reinvested returns. This approach can help them work towards key financial goals, from retirement planning and buying a home to funding a child’s education.What is compounding?Compounding lets investors earn returns not only on their initial investment but also on gains they've accumulated over time. This creates a snowball effect, as those returns generate further gains. The longer the money stays invested, the greater the potential benefit.Also Read |Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund added DLF, Bharti Airtel, Indus Towers and 10 other stocks to its portfolio in September. Details here How SIPs harness the power of compoundingSIP is a disciplined way to invest a fixed amount regularly—monthly, quarterly, or even weekly—in a mutual fund scheme. While SIPs help average out market volatility through rupee cost averaging, their true magic lies in how they make compounding work more efficiently over time.By investing consistently through SIPs, even small amounts can grow significantly due to the compounding effect. Each SIP instalment earns returns, and those returns are reinvested and continue to earn more. The longer you stay invested, the more the compounding effect multiplies your wealth.Example: Power of compoundingYou start a SIP of Rs 10,000 per month, and the mutual fund gives an average annual return of 12%. You plan to invest for 20 years.The yearly SIP investment - Rs 10,000 × 12 months = Rs 1,20,000 per yearThe total investment period -  20 yearsRs 1,20,000 × 20 = Rs 24,00,000The maturity amount after 20 years at 12% return using SIP compound interest formula or calculator = Rs 99,90,000 (approximately Rs1 crore)Amount you invested: Rs 24,00,000Wealth created through compounding: Rs 75,90,000% of return through compounding: approximately 76% of the total maturity valueHere, compounding has worked quietly in the background, helping you build more than four times your actual investment.Also Read |ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: REITs can diversify portfolios, but total returns matter, says Ramesh NairWhy time matters more than the amount you investMany investors delay investing because they think they need a large amount to begin. But with compounding, time in the market matters more than timing the market. Starting early—even with a small SIP—can yield better results than starting late with a larger amount.How to maximise the benefits of compounding through SIPsThe most important thing to do for compounding through SIPs is to start early, as the earlier you begin, the more time your money has to grow. Secondly, one should stay consistent, which means not stopping SIPs due to short-term market volatility.Thirdly, stay invested for the long term because compounding rewards patience. Lastly, increase the SIP amount over time, which means gradually raising your SIP as your income grows to enhance your corpus.SIPs are one of the most convenient and effective ways to benefit from the power of compounding. They make market investing simple for everyone—from beginners to seasoned investors. By starting early, staying invested, and being consistent, you can put compounding to work and create meaningful wealth over time.One should always remember that it's not just how much you invest, but how long you stay invested that truly makes the difference.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. articles.title: Delhi protest: What's happening today?
articles.summary: Security has been tightened across Delhi ahead of a planned protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and INDIA bloc at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10. The demonstration is aimed at demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. Police have detained more than 150 people, while restrictions on Metro services, internet access and road traffic have affected movement across parts of the national capital.Delhi protest: Dhruv Rathee among those detainedYouTuber Dhruv Rathee has been detained by Delhi Police from his residence in Sector 56, Gurugram, sources told news agency PTI.The Cockroach Janta Party also claimed on X that Rathee had been detained, alleging that the government was afraid of young people who questioned its actions.CJP's legal head Ratna Singh was also reportedly detained from her Delhi residence, according to media reports.Meanwhile, police detained more than 200 protesters on Saturday morning ahead of the planned demonstration. Earlier, a few protesters who had started gathering at Jantar Mantar were also detained.The detentions came amid heightened security arrangements across Delhi, with police checking vehicles at border points and deploying personnel at key locations to prevent unauthorised gatherings.Nitin Nabin accuses INDIA bloc, CJP of trying to destabilise IndiaBJP president Nitin Nabin accused the INDIA bloc, led by Rahul Gandhi, and the CJP of attempting to create instability in the country.In his remarks, Nabin described the two groups as anarchic and alleged that they were competing to create unrest instead of accepting the public's electoral verdict. He further alleged that their political activities were being carried out at the behest of foreign forces, but did not provide evidence for the claim in the quoted remarks.— ANI (@ANI) Nabin also said India was progressing despite global crises and accused the Opposition of being unable to accept the country's growth and movement towards self-reliance.He asserted that Indian democracy was strong and that citizens would unite to thwart attempts to destabilise the country.Why is CJP protesting at Jantar Mantar?The CJP has called for a demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.The protest comes amid an escalating political confrontation between the Opposition and the Election Commission of India over allegations of 'vote chori' and concerns surrounding the revision of electoral rolls.Delhi Police denied permission for the demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing a previous breakdown of law and order in the area.CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke criticised the government's response to the planned protest, alleging that authorities were attempting to discourage people from participating.Speaking to reporters in Mumbai before leaving for Delhi, Dipke accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being afraid of young people who question the government. He also alleged that police personnel were visiting residential areas to discourage residents from joining the demonstration.Dipke maintained that peaceful protest was a fundamental right under Article 19 of the Constitution.Delhi Metro closes gates at 45 stationsThe Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) announced restrictions at 45 Metro stations in view of the planned demonstration and the associated security arrangements.Entry and exit gates at the affected stations were closed from 9 pm on Friday, October 9, with the restrictions scheduled to continue through Saturday evening.The measures were intended to manage crowds and maintain security around sensitive locations in the national capital. The restrictions have also affected access to stations in areas surrounding the planned protest.Commuters have been advised to check official Delhi Metro updates before travelling, as services and access arrangements may change depending on the security situation.Delhi Airport issues travel advisoryDelhi Airport has advised passengers travelling to and from the airport to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional time for their commute.The advisory was issued amid heightened security arrangements and anticipated traffic restrictions linked to the protest.“In view of the enhanced security arrangements and anticipated traffic restrictions in Delhi, passengers travelling to and from Delhi Airport are advised to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional time for their commute,” the airport said in a statement.It also advised passengers to consider alternative transport options, including cabs and city buses, where appropriate.Delhi Traffic Police separately advised commuters to keep extra travel time if heading towards railway stations, inter-state bus terminals (ISBTs) or the airport through New Delhi and Central Delhi.People were also advised to avoid non-essential travel. The police said traffic management arrangements could be adjusted based on real-time assessments of the situation.Internet services suspended near Janpath and Kartavya PathAuthorities have imposed additional restrictions in parts of central Delhi, including a temporary suspension of internet services around the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing.Internet services were suspended within a radius of 4 km from the crossing for 24 hours, starting at 10 pm on Friday, October 9.The area is considered sensitive because of its proximity to key government buildings and other important locations.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) has also been imposed in Delhi as authorities step up security ahead of the demonstration.Separately, Gautam Buddh Nagar Police imposed prohibitory orders across the district from Saturday morning until October 20. The restrictions prohibit gatherings of five or more people without prior permission, processions, provocative speeches and the spread of misleading information.Security tightened at Delhi borders and key locationsDelhi Police remained on high alert on Saturday, with security strengthened across the national capital and vehicle checks intensified at inter-state and inter-district borders.Police personnel were deployed at several entry points, including the Aya Nagar, Ghazipur and Badarpur borders. Barricades were installed at multiple locations, while personnel checked vehicles entering Delhi.Deputy Commissioner of Police Anant Mittal visited the Aya Nagar border to review security arrangements.Speaking to news agency IANS, Mittal said special arrangements had been made at inter-state and inter-district borders to prevent unauthorised elements from entering New Delhi and to maintain law and order.Police personnel were also equipped with body cameras to record incidents and help monitor any physical altercations during the demonstration.Drone surveillance was underway at key locations, including New Delhi Railway Station, where Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed. Security marches were also conducted.Security was strengthened outside the residences of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. Additional security personnel were deployed at sensitive locations, while roads leading towards Janpath and Mandi House witnessed barricading and checks.Train cancellations inconvenience passengersSeveral trains were cancelled amid the heightened security arrangements, causing inconvenience to passengers travelling to and from Delhi on Saturday.Passengers at railway stations reported having to change their travel plans at short notice.One passenger told IANS that trains running via Jaunpur, including the Tapti Ganga and Kashi Vishwanath Express, had been cancelled. The passenger said they might have to travel to Lucknow and change trains or take a bus to reach their destination.Another passenger travelling from Gujarat said they had faced difficulties reaching Ghaziabad after arriving at Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station, as the expected connecting trains were unavailable.However, some passengers reported that their journeys had continued without difficulty, with trains arriving at Hazrat Nizamuddin on time.Police and Rapid Action Force personnel remained deployed at railway stations, while drone surveillance and security patrols continued.Delhi protest: What should commuters keep in mind?With security measures in force across Delhi and neighbouring areas, commuters should check the latest official advisories before setting out.Metro: Check DMRC updates for restrictions on entry and exit gates at affected stations.Airport: Allow extra time for travel and consider alternative transport options.Roads: Check Delhi Traffic Police advisories before travelling through central Delhi or towards railway stations and ISBTs.Trains: Verify train status with the relevant railway authorities before leaving for the station.Internet: Be aware of the reported temporary suspension of internet services in parts of central Delhi.Authorities have said that security and traffic arrangements may be modified depending on the situation on the ground. The restrictions come as police prepare to manage the planned demonstration while maintaining law and order across the national capital.
